Fallback recovery formatting

Height reservation for deep recovery chains · per-lane cascade · hover-only insert icons · arrowheads at every convergence landing — 2026-09-06, worktree agent-a1eb15213ee582e7b, uncommitted.

What Zach reported

Filed on the failure-branch-formatting board with an annotated screenshot of his literal PickAndPlace tree — a flat Fallback whose recovery chain is MoveHome →Failure→ GraspValid →Failure→ (CorrectGrip → GraspValid re-check): “you are not spacing the height correctly … by the 3rd branch you are getting a lot of overlap — you need to account for the height of the last branch in the other 2 branches.” Plus two visual rules: “ICONS SHOW ONLY ON HOVER” and “Note the arrow ends” — three junctions circled in green, each pasted over with an arrowhead crop (the junction one rotated 90°, pointing along the merge line into the rail).

Shipped — his literal tree, in the real app

“Note the arrow ends” — his three circles, shipped

Edge structure in lanesWithRecovery: each arm's return is a drop edge (merge:<i>, arrowEnd: true) plus one shared straight run (merge:run, arrowEnd: true) from the farthest landing to the junction — not per-lane overlapping polylines — and the primary's own merge:rail drop stays headless. Pinned per nesting level and both orientations by layouts.test.ts “marks every convergence landing with an arrowhead”.

The cascade — the piece still missing this morning

The rewritten reservation already computed the merge line one unit below the deepest arm (Zach's “account for the last branch up front”), but placed every sibling arm at one shared height. For a flat multi-arm Fallback that put the 2nd arm's Failure corner inside its first card — the line entered from below, chip half-hidden. laneBoxFlow is now a per-lane array: every arm's box one unit below the Failure line that feeds it, that line leaving the previous arm at its mid-height — so every arm is entered from above, exactly his mockup. Pinned by “enters every arm from above, through its top face, by exactly one unit” + a failure-chip/card clearance sweep, on his literal tree shape.

“Icons show only on hover” — recorded, not asserted

Decision surface

Done and proved

  • Height reservation accounts for the deepest branch up front — 3-level nested and flat 3-arm trees lay out with zero overlap (1506/1506 unit, 85/85 journey checks).
  • Per-lane cascade restored: every arm entered from above, chips clear of cards — on your literal PickAndPlace shape, in the real app.
  • Arrowheads at all three circled convergence points; single straight merge line preserved byte-for-byte in spirit: one run, headless rail continuation.
  • Interior “+” hover-only with per-zone reveal; persistent start/terminus exemption kept.

Needs you

  • Walk the review board (URL above). Default if you say nothing: this stays as-is on the worktree branch, un-merged — nothing lands on main without your word.
  • The junction arrowhead points along the merge line into the rail (your rotated crop, circle 1). If you meant a down-arrow on the rail below the junction instead, it is a one-line arrowEnd flip on merge:rail.

Deliberately not done

  • No “thick tick mark” glyph distinct from the arrowheads — your pasted crops were arrowheads, so arrowheads are what shipped.
  • Blackboard/Dataflow lens edges keep their existing arrow rules; only the recovery/merge family changed.
  • The peer tasks in this worktree (arrow live-tracking + spacing slider, dnd-kit migration) are untouched and report separately; their known open item (wire.settles-on-drop) is theirs.
